english: Once there was no night. The Twin and his sister were alone. Then the Twin died, the first of mortals. His sister sat beside the body; she cried and did not eat. Her tears flowed onto the body. The gods said to her: "Forget your brother." She said: "My brother is gone." The sun did not go down, and she did not forget. Then the gods put night between the days. Black night came, and the stars and the moon flashed up. The sister slept. In the morning Dawn grew bright, and the sister forgot her grief. In the night mortals forget grief.

english: The Twin is the first of mortals who died. No one followed him. Below, in the darkness, he sought the path. He crossed the black river by the ford, and the cold current came up to his knees. An eagle flew before him and showed him the ford. On the other side he found a broad pasture. There cows eat sweet grass. In the pasture he sat down and became king of the dead. He found the path for many, the path which our dead went. That path our grandsons will go. A mortal does not flee from death.

english: Yonder flows a black river. No man swims through it, and no fish lives in it. An old man waits at the ford with a boat. He carries the dead over the water. He takes a wage from the dead: bronze. He questions each dead man: "Whose son are you?" The dead man says the name of his parent. Then he carries him in the boat. Whoever does not know his own lineage stays here in the cold, crying. So a man teaches his boy his lineage.

She speaks: "I am your good mind and your good word." She leads him to the house of song.
